stories.headline: GPS tracking helps reduce garbage black spots in Bengaluru's Bommanahalli
stories.deck: GPS tracking helps reduce garbage black spots in Bommanahalli
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: A pilot project using GPS tracking on garbage collection auto tippers has helped reduce black spots in Bommanahalli, the Bengaluru South City Corporation (BSCC) has claimed..On August 13, GPS trackers were installed on 36 garbage collection autos at Atal Bihari Vajpayee Stadium in HSR Layout..According to the BSCC, residents and NGOs have reported a considerable reduction in black spots over the past three weeks following daily door-to-door waste collection..30 tonnes of garbage, construction waste cleared near Tagore statue in R T Nagar.The BSCC now plans to extend the system to all 208 garbage collection autos in Bommanahalli..Commissioner KN Ramesh has directed officials to complete the installation by September 10 and begin full-scale tracking across the Bommanahalli Assembly constituency from September 11..‘Brain Above’ app.Once GPS tracking and route mapping are completed across its nine wards, residents will be able to track the autos assigned to their streets and access other details through the ‘Brain Above’ app, Ramesh said..In narrow lanes inaccessible to autos, vehicles will stop at nearby points for 10 minutes and collect household waste by blowing whistles, he added..Ramesh has also directed contractors to deploy garbage collection autos at night in and around high-density black spots. Shopkeepers in commercial areas will be given two to three days to start handing over waste to night-shift autos. Continued violations will attract a nominal fine initially, followed by heavier fines and vehicle seizure for repeat offences, he said.

stories.headline: ISRO successfully launches Earth observation satellite EOS-05
stories.deck: The EOS-05 is India’s first ever imaging satellite to monitor from Geosynchronous orbit about 36,000 km above the Earth.
stories.bodyText:
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), which has had a quiet year so far, is back to winning ways with the successful launch of the state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft, EOS-05.
The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) on its 19th flight placed the EOS-05 into the intended Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit 18 minutes after it lifted off from the second launch pad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota at 2.55 a.m. on September 4.
The EOS-05 is India’s first ever imaging satellite to monitor from Geosynchronous orbit about 36,000 km above the Earth.
“I am very happy to announce that the GSLV-F17 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the advanced Earth observation satellite EOS-05 in the intended and required orbit, “ ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said.
He added that this was the 107th launch from the spaceport in Sriharikota and 19th mission of the GSLV.
“The first launch of the GSLV- D1 was done with a payload of 1536 kg from that gradually we have improved the performance of this vehicle by optimising the structural mass, improving the propulsion systems and today we have injected the heaviest satellite, a 2367 kg satellite using this launch vehicle,” he added.
The ISRO Chairman said that once the Earth observation satellite, EOS-05 is operationalised in orbit it will become India’s first dedicated imaging satellite from the Geo Orbit providing important strategic data for our country.
“From the satellite data we confirm all the valves are operating perfectly, the solar panel is deployed and the health of the satellite is perfectly alright.
In the coming days we will raise the orbit and take it to the required orbit and place the satellite in the Geo platform for national activities,” the ISRO Chairman said.
The EOS-05 satellite dubbed as Eye in the Sky will provide real-time imagery besides helping agriculture, environment, disaster management among others.
The successful launch of the EOS-05 comes as a huge relief for ISRO which has not carried out any launch activities since the failure of the PSLV-C62 mission carrying the EOS-N1 earth observation satellite on January 12, 2026.
The space agency since the back to back failures of PSLV-C62 and the PSLV-C61 in May 18, 2025 had taken a cautious approach and refrained from carrying out any launches.
Though seven missions including the GSLV-F17/EOS-05 were scheduled to take place in the first quarter of 2026, ISRO did not lauch any satellites.
The successful launch of the 2367 kg EOS-05 satellite, also puts behind the failure which ISRO had encountered in August 2021 with the GSLV-F10 / EOS-03 mission.
Back then, the GSLV-F10 / EOS-03’s mission performance was normal during the first and second stages. However, the cryogenic upper stage ignition did not happen due to a technical anomaly, and the mission remained unsuccessful. The EOS-05 satellite replaces the unsuccessful EOS-03 mission.
Published - September 04, 2026 03:05 am IST

stories.headline: Spoilt eggs found at Blinkit stock unit in Mangaluru
stories.deck: Following a complaint from a consumer to Health Minister U.T. Khader, food safety inspectors from the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department conducted an inspection at a Blinkit stock and supply unit
stories.bodyText:
Following a complaint from a consumer to Health Minister U.T. Khader, food safety inspectors from the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department conducted an inspection at a Blinkit stock and supply unit in Falnir Square, Hampanakatta, Mangaluru.
Mr. Khader said, “I received a complaint from a consumer about eggs containing germs. The consumer had also shared a receipt from Blinkit, and the order had been placed on September 1, 2026. I directed department officials to inspect the unit. Several broken and spoiled eggs were found during the inspection.”
He added, “A warning has been issued to the unit manager, and all the eggs were destroyed after a complete inspection.”

stories.headline: 'Iran conflict is not a war, declines to offer timeline for end': J D Vance
stories.bodyText: WASHINGTON: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday said the fighting between the United States and Iran was not a war and declined to provide a timeline for when the conflict would be over, underscoring the challenge the Trump administration faces as the hostilities enter their seventh month and midterm elections loom.His comments come as Washington and Tehran exchanged back-and-forth attacks this week after a period of relative calm, with no diplomatic talks with the Iranians underway to end the conflict.The war has dragged down President Donald Trump's approval ratings and driven up gas prices, raising the stakes for Republican candidates fighting to preserve their party's narrow congressional majorities in November..Iran war escalation raises concern over civilian death toll.In a briefing at the White House, Vance touted U.S. efforts to facilitate oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranians have disrupted maritime traffic since the war started, crediting Washington's actions with helping to avert a broader global energy crisis.He pushed back on describing the conflict as a "war," saying the U.S. has ended major combat operations with Iran, despite renewed fighting this week. He said Washington's focus now was to ensure Tehran cannot keep disrupting commercial oil shipping."I wouldn't call it a war," Vance said. "Right now there's no active shooting. I recognize there's been places where this has flared up."The U.S. maintains more than 50,000 troops in the Middle East. The Trump administration has surged assets into the region, including nearly 20 warships focused on a blockade. In some instances, troops have been deployed for longer than expected and have been pulled from Europe and the Indo-Pacific.Asked repeatedly about the timeline on the war, Vance said an end would require a halt in Iranians shooting at commercial shipping."When will the Iranians stop shooting at ships? I think the reality is I don't know the answer to that question," he said.He also ruled out any negotiations as long as Tehran continued to target commercial shipping.While the most intense fighting has subsided, the recurring exchange of fire and the lack of a definitive end to the war have kept global oil prices elevated.On Tuesday, the United States launched airstrikes on Iran, hitting what it said were military targets along the coast in retaliation for Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The sudden escalation of the war has caused a surge in oil prices to levels unseen since July.

stories.headline: Mandhana scripts history, surpasses Mithali Raj to become highest run-scorer
stories.deck: Smriti Mandhana has made history as the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket, breaking Mithali Raj's enduring record during the Asia Cup. Her extraordinary performance included a remarkable 124 runs off just 64 balls, establishing new benchmarks for both individual scores and partnerships. This milestone is a pivotal moment, showcasing the evolution and rise of women's cricket on…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Smriti Mandhana
 has already established herself among the finest batters in women's cricket, but on Thursday she reached a new pinnacle — becoming the most prolific run-scorer in the history of the women's game.
During India's Women's Asia Cup 2026 clash against Hong Kong China in Dubai, the Indian vice-captain surpassed legendary former captain 
Mithali Raj
's tally of 10,868 international runs to become the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket across all formats.
And she did it in spectacular fashion.
Mandhana produced a breathtaking 124 off 64 balls, smashing 14 fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 193.75 as India posted 193/5 after being asked to bat first. Her record-breaking innings not only took her past Mithali but also established a series of new milestones.
Mandhana goes past Mithali in style
Mandhana entered the match knowing she was closing in on Mithali's long-standing record. Having already overtaken New Zealand great Suzie Bates to move into second place during the Asia Cup opener against Thailand, the 30-year-old needed one more major push to rewrite the all-time record.
She delivered far more than that.
Mandhana initially had to negotiate a slow Dubai surface and disciplined Hong Kong bowling. Shafali Verma provided the early acceleration, with the opening pair putting on 50 before Verma departed for 28 off 17 balls.
Once Mandhana settled in, however, the innings changed gears.
She reached her half-century and then launched an extraordinary assault, moving from 50 to 100 in just 17 deliveries. Her century came off 57 balls before she eventually finished with 124 from 64, her second T20I hundred.
Her dismissal came on the final over of the innings following a mix-up with Bharti Fulmali, but by then Mandhana had already rewritten the record books.
The 124 also became the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119 against Malaysia in 2024.
Most runs in Women’s international cricket
- 10880* - Smriti Mandhana
- 10868 - Mithali Raj
- 10740 - Suzie Bates
- 10273 - Charlotte Edwards
- 10007 - Stafanie Taylor
From Mithali's record to a pile of milestones
Mandhana's landmark innings did not stop with the all-time runs record.
Her century took her international hundred tally to 18, making her the leading century-maker in women's international cricket, ahead of Australia's Meg Lanning and South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt, who had 17 each.
She also became the first Indian woman to score two T20I centuries. Her previous hundred had come against England in 2025, when she made 112.
The latest innings also extended Mandhana and Shafali's remarkable partnership record. Their 50-plus stand against Hong Kong was their 29th in T20Is, the most by any pair in the format.
ALSO READ: Smriti Mandhana equals Mithali Raj’s big record, then creates more history
For Mandhana, though, the most significant achievement was undoubtedly moving past Mithali.
Mithali's 10,868 runs had stood as the benchmark of women's international batting excellence since her retirement in 2022. Mandhana's explosive rise has now taken her beyond that mark, with New Zealand's Suzie Bates, England's Charlotte Edwards and West Indies great Stafanie Taylor completing the top five on the all-time list.
What made Thursday's achievement even more remarkable was the manner in which Mandhana reached it. On a surface that offered little pace, she adapted her game, used the back foot effectively and found ways to manufacture boundaries.
“Having said that, I just love batting, and I’m happy that I could contribute,” Mandhana said during the mid-innings break.

briefs.headline: U.S. hits Cuba with new sanctions as island’s crises multiply
briefs.deck: The sanctions aim to push Cuba’s critical machinery offline and exacerbate its energy crisis, said Brett Erickson, a sanctions expert and managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, a consulting firm
briefs.bodyText:
The U.S. government on Thursday (September 3, 2026) slapped new sanctions on Cuba in a fresh push to strangle the island’s economy and deepen its multiple crises.
Among those hit with sanctions are Fidel Ernesto Castro, grandson of former President Raúl Castro, and Cuba’s Oil Industry Supply Import Company, known as Abapet. The company is responsible for importing special equipment and spare parts needed to sustain Cuba’s crumbling power grid.
The sanctions aim to push Cuba’s critical machinery offline and exacerbate its energy crisis, said Brett Erickson, a sanctions expert and managing principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, a consulting firm.
“The U.S. is trying to really tighten the screws as much as possible,” he said.
“The Trump administration seems to have no seriousness to accept any change from Cuba other than a toppling of regime. Marco is not going to let that go,” he added, referring to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Mr. Erickson anticipated that Cuba’s government would try to circumvent the sanctions “because they have to.”
“They’ll get creative in how they try to procure these maintenance parts,” he said, warning it would be a costlier alternative, which in turn would raise inflation and further hurt Cuba’s economy.
Islandwide blackouts have become increasingly common, while daily outages in Cuba now surpass 24 hours as the aging grid fails and fuel reserves dwindle ever since U.S. President Donald Trump in late January threatened tariffs on any country that sells or provides oil to the island.
“The goal in theory is to create so much civilian hardship and suffering that they have no option but to essentially rise up and topple their government,” Mr. Erickson said. “It is an attempt to cause a humanitarian crisis.”
Talks earlier this year between the U.S. and Cuba have since halted, while sanctions have increased in recent months.
Mr. Erickson said he expects the U.S. to keep targeting smaller and smaller state companies to try and push them “into a death spiral.” The U.S. has previously sanctioned entities including Cuba's state-owned oil and gas company.
The U.S. State Department made the announcement just hours after Cuban officials held a press conference to share more details on the historic economic reforms approved in June.
When asked about the current situation in Cuba, Oscar Pérez-Oliva Fraga, Cuba’s deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Investment, blamed the U.S. government.
“This past year has been very complex, and we know why,” he said. “The blockade is a genocide.”
He spoke before the sanctions were announced.
Among the Cubans exhausted by the ongoing outages is 49-year-old Yaqueline Bernal. She said on Thursday (September 3) that she hasn’t had electricity since Sunday (August 30) and worries most about the consequences for her eight young grandchildren.
“If we don’t have power, we don’t have water,” she said. “You really don’t know what’s going to happen to you.”
Bruno Rodríguez, Cuba's Foreign Affairs Minister, decried the latest sanctions on X.
“Collective punishment is a crime. So, too, is inflicting suffering on an entire population through measures coldly calculated to trigger a humanitarian crisis,” he said. “Enough with the abuse. Put an end to the blockade once and for all and allow Cuba to live in peace.”
Eugenio Martínez Enríquez, Cuba’s ambassador in Mexico, called Mr. Rubio “a liar without scruples.”
“We will not forget his crimes,” he wrote on X.
Meanwhile, Mr. Rubio asserted on X that those sanctioned “are part of the corrupt Castro financial and intelligence network.”
“Cuba’s Communist regime elites preside over a failed state where ordinary Cubans go hungry while the Castro family and other insiders enrich themselves through sanctions evasion and other illicit schemes — and seek to export subversive Marxist ideology to the United States and other states in the Western Hemisphere,” he wrote.
“Trump and I are unwavering in our commitment that Cuba will be free.”

briefs.headline: FBI puts India-born man on most wanted fraudsters list
briefs.bodyText: Washington: The FBI has added India-born Manjit Singh Bedi to its list of most wanted fraudsters for his alleged involvement in irregularities in the US government's benefits scheme..According to the FBI, Bedi operated a small grocery store in Tacoma, Washington, and swiped customers' government benefits cards to give them cash instead of food under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Programme (SNAP)..Instead of selling food to participants, Bedi allegedly swiped their Electronic Benefit Transfer cards and gave them cash, keeping half of the proceeds for himself, the FBI said on Thursday. The FBI claimed that Bedi, a naturalised US citizen, defrauded the US government of at least USD 6 lakh between March 2024 and June 2025..Bedi operated a small grocery store in Tacoma called Asian Grocery Store. He purportedly sold food to SNAP participants using their EBT cards..'Most wanted': FBI offers $50,000 reward for info on gangster Goldy Brar, aide of Lawrence Bishnoi.“A reward of up to USD 150,000 is offered for information leading to his arrest and conviction,” the FBI said..After being indicted for wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud, Bedi was allowed to appear in court without being arrested..He was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state..However, Bedi soon drove across the border to Canada and then fled to India, the FBI said..A federal arrest warrant was issued for Bedi on May 21 in a US district court after he was charged with Violations of Conditions of Supervision.

briefs.headline: Work on uncrewed Gaganyaan mission in full swing: ISRO chief Narayanan
briefs.bodyText: Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh): ISRO chief V Narayanan on Friday said that "vigorous, systematic work," is on for the launch of the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission during this calendar year..The launch of the earth observation satellite (GSLV-F17/EOS-05) is the first success for ISRO during this financial year, Narayanan said adding, "reward for hard work is more work." Accordingly, the ISRO team, along with industries and other organisations, is working on the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission..In his address following the successful launch of EOS-05, he said that activities were underway very "vigorously and systematically," for the uncrewed mission launch during this calendar year..NASA invites ISRO to be part of plan for setting up first human outpost on Moon.Praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his leadership, Narayanan said that six more launches, including the navigation satellite NVS-03, are targeted for this financial year..Later, addressing a press conference, the ISRO chief said the earth observation satellite's operational lifetime is nine years and dismissed speculations that it was a "spy satellite."

briefs.headline: 38 people rescued after ferry breaks down off Gateway of India in Mumbai
briefs.bodyText: Mumbai: Police and a local boat operator rescued 38 people, including 34 passengers, after a ferry suffered a mid-sea engine breakdown off the Gateway of India on Thursday night, an official said..The incident occurred around 8.30 pm when 'Anwari', which operates half-hour sea excursions, was returning to the Gateway of India and broke down some 1.5 nautical miles off the coast, he said..The boat was carrying 34 passengers and four crew members..Diesel boats at Gateway of India to go electric under govt scheme, says Nitish Rane.Upon receiving an alert from the police control room, Constable Abhijit Shinde and other personnel inquired about other boats operating in the vicinity..Learning that another excursion vessel, 'Azad Hind', was near the stranded boat, the officers contacted its owner Junaid Mulla and sought his help..The 'Azad Hind' reached the spot and towed 'Anwari' safely to Jetty no. 2 at the Gateway of India by 9.30 pm..All 34 passengers and four crew members were safely brought ashore without any injuries, the official said.

briefs.headline: CBI books Delhi man for posing as PMO official
briefs.bodyText: New Delhi: The CBI has registered a case against a South Delhi resident who was allegedly posing as a Prime Minister's Office (PMO) official to secure preferential emergency treatment at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), officials said..It is alleged in the complaint filed by the PMO that Ravi Kant Sharma, a Sangam Vihar resident, falsely claimed to be an Officer on Special Duty to the Prime Minister to pressure B N Acharya, a protocol officer at AIIMS, to arrange a priority emergency admission and treatment for a patient at the crowded prestigious Institute..Himachal Pradesh man booked for securing accountant's job with fake BA degree in Bengaluru.The PMO confirmed that Sharma was never employed as an Officer on Special Duty..The CBI also found that Sharma had used the ruse to obtain priority hospital services for other patients, which were accorded to him as hospital staff believed him to be an authorised official. briefs.headline: West Asia war updates: Iran media says six navy personnel killed in U.S. attacks
briefs.deck: According to a media report, it wasn’t immediately clear if the six naval personnel were among the seven already reported dead in Khuzestan
briefs.bodyText:
Iran’s Tasnim news agency on Thursday (September 3, 2026) said six members of the Iranian Army’s naval forces were killed by U.S. attacks during renewed fighting this week. “The six died during a wave of U.S. attacks on Tuesday (September 1, 2026),” the report said, without specifying where they were killed.
“Seven people were killed in the southwestern province of Khuzestan, and four members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard died in Kermanshah province,” Iranian media said. “Three paramilitaries were killed on Lavan island in the Gulf and another died in Fars province,” they said. It wasn’t immediately clear if the six naval personnel were among the seven already reported dead in Khuzestan.
Earlier in the day, Iran attacked U.S. military bases in Kuwait, despite President Donald Trump threatening further strikes in a fresh flare-up six months into the war. Mr. Trump said his military was prepared to attack Iran “any time we want” after extensive US bombardment of sites across the country left at least 19 Iranians dead.
Tehran retaliated by hitting U.S. military targets across West Asia, including in Kuwait, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region.

briefs.headline: How Abhishek Sharma conquered the fastest format to reach a record T20I rating
briefs.deck: Abhishek Sharma has reached unprecedented heights in the ICC T20I realm, obtaining the highest batting rating ever recorded. After impressing in domestic cricket, he secured a regular place on the Indian team. Under the guidance of Yuvraj Singh, his dynamic batting style flourished, leading to remarkable achievements in runs and strike rate throughout a calendar year.
briefs.bodyText:
Abhishek Sharma has come a long way from the little boy in Amritsar who first picked up a cricket bat at the age of three-and-a-half. On his birthday, his journey stands out as one of the most remarkable rises in modern T20 cricket, from a promising youngster in Punjab to an India regular and the holder of the highest-ever ICC T20I batting rating.
The boy who started cricket at three-and-a-half
Abhishek's father, Raj Kumar Sharma, a former cricketer, introduced him to the game when he was just three-and-a-half. The youngster quickly developed an obsession with batting and progressed through Punjab's age-group system.
His numbers soon began attracting attention. During the 2015-16 Vijay Merchant Trophy, Abhishek scored more than 1,200 runs at an average of 109.09 and also claimed 57 wickets. He captained Punjab to the Under-19 Asia Cup title in 2016 before becoming part of India's victorious Under-19 World Cup campaign in 2018.
The IPL came at just 17, when Delhi Daredevils picked him in the 2018 auction. His career, however, did not explode immediately. Abhishek spent several seasons developing his game through domestic cricket and the IPL before finding the perfect platform for his aggressive style.
Yuvraj Singh's influence shapes his fearless approach
A major influence during that period was Yuvraj Singh. The former India all-rounder became Abhishek's mentor and worked closely with him, particularly during the Covid-19 lockdown. 
Yuvraj understood the youngster's attacking instincts and encouraged him to embrace them rather than become overly cautious. That philosophy eventually became the foundation of Abhishek's T20 game.
His international breakthrough came after making his T20I debut in July 2024. In February 2025, Abhishek produced one of the most devastating T20I innings by an Indian batter when he smashed 135 off just 54 balls against England in Mumbai. The innings contained 13 sixes and a 37-ball century, announcing him as one of India's most dangerous T20 batters.
From breakthrough star to world-record holder
The 135 was only the beginning. During the 2025 Asia Cup, Abhishek established himself as India's attacking force at the top of the order. He scored 314 runs in seven matches at a strike rate of 200 and was named Player of the Tournament as India won the competition.
His performances pushed him to the top of the ICC T20I batting rankings and eventually into record-breaking territory. After scoring 61 against Sri Lanka, Abhishek reached 931 rating points, the highest-ever rating achieved by a men's T20I batter.
He surpassed Dawid Malan's previous record of 919 and moved beyond the best ratings achieved by India's Suryakumar Yadav and Virat Kohli.
A T20 batter built for destruction
The numbers behind Abhishek's rise were extraordinary. In 2025, he became the first player to score more than 1,000 runs in T20 cricket in a calendar year while maintaining a strike rate above 200. He finished the year at a strike rate of 202 and smashed 108 sixes.
His IPL performances were equally destructive. Playing for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Abhishek produced a stunning 141 off 55 balls against Punjab Kings in IPL 2025. He reached his fifty in only 16 balls and his century in 40, hitting 14 fours and 10 sixes as Hyderabad chased down 246. The innings broke KL Rahul's record for the highest score by an Indian batter in IPL history.
His development has been shaped by several influential figures. Apart from Yuvraj, Abhishek has drawn lessons from players such as Shikhar Dhawan, Brian Lara and Travis Head. At Sunrisers, his partnership with Head showed how effectively his aggressive approach could work against the best bowling attacks.
At the 2026 T20 World Cup, Abhishek added another major achievement to his growing list, playing a crucial role in India's title-winning campaign, including a blistering 52 off 21 balls in the final against New Zealand.
T20I career so far 
Abhishek Sharma has played 56 T20Is between 2024 and 2026, scoring 1,629 runs in 55 innings at an average of 30.73 and a remarkable strike rate of 187.24. He has registered two centuries and 11 fifties, with a highest score of 135. His aggressive approach is reflected in his boundary count, with the left-hander hitting 164 fours and 104 sixes in his international career so far.

stories.headline: Bengaluru landlord booked for not verifying credentials of 3 Bangladeshi tenants
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A routine police patrol led to the detection of three Bangladeshi nationals staying in a rented house in northeast Bengaluru without proper tenant verification.
According to police, around 8pm on Aug 23, a patrol officer received information that GV Rekha, owner of a building in New Mico Layout, had rented out the second floor to Bangladeshi nationals without carrying out mandatory police or tenant verification.
A police team visited the house and questioned the occupants, identified as Salma Begum, 26, Munna Faraji, 21, and Hafeezah, 19. Police said all three provided an address in Bagerhat district of Bangladesh.
The tenants were directed to appear before police the following morning and were subsequently produced before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) for verification.
FRRO confirmed they were Bangladeshi nationals. Following the FRRO order, police filed a suo motu case against the property owner under the Foreigners Act. Investigation is in progress.

stories.headline: PIL against tunnel: Karnataka high court seeks engineer’s presentation on Hebbal lake impact
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The high court Thursday adjourned to next week the hearing on a PIL challenging the proposed short tunnel project at Hebbal Lake, directing the authorities to arrange a presentation by an engineer to demonstrate that the project would not disturb the water body’s inflow and outflow.
A division bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice KS Hemalekha observed that such a presentation could allay the petitioners’ concerns that the project would drain the lake.
Appearing for RK Guruprasad and two other petitioners, advocate Sneha Nagaraj submitted that lake land had been diverted for the tunnel project. She contended that the construction would obstruct the lake’s inlet and outlet, a fact reflected in documents available with the authorities.
On the other hand, Advocate General Shashikiran Shetty maintained that the project would not affect the lake’s inflow or outflow. He agreed to the court’s request to arrange a technical presentation by an engineer explaining the measures proposed to ensure that the water body’s flow remains undisturbed.
The petitioners have sought quashing of the project’s DPR, titled “Short Length Transitory 3-Lane Bi-Directional Vehicular Underpass connecting Hebbal Flyover Junction to Veterinary College via GKVK campus premises,” prepared pursuant to the revised final draft report of Sept 2025, along with all consequential actions initiated based on it.
They have also sought a declaration that the Karnataka Tank Conservation and Development Authority (Amendment) Act, to the extent it reduces buffer zones, is unconstitutional. They further seek striking down of Rule 24 of the BMLTA Rules, which exempts the project from the prior approval required under the BMLTA Act.
HC seeks GSI report on Lalbagh
Meanwhile, the division bench directed the state govt to place before the court a Geological Survey of India report on the Peninsular Gneissic Complex concerning Lalbagh.
The direction came after Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya, appearing as counsel, urged the court to call for the report.
The hearing on a PIL filed by Dr Adikesavalu Ravindra, theatre personality Prakash Belawadi and others challenging the 16.7-km twin-tunnel project was adjourned to Sept 10. The petitioners have challenged the July 14, 2025 tender notification issued by the govt and the erstwhile BBMP (now GBA), along with various project-related communications, the Dec 2024 feasibility study report and the Detailed Project Report (DPR) issued in Feb-March this year.
According to the petitioners, the project, estimated to cost between Rs 17,780 crore and Rs 19,000 crore, has been advanced without a lawful assessment of its economic viability, social impact and constitutional validity.

stories.headline: Citizens term withdrawal of Parks Bill ‘victory for Bengaluru’
stories.deck: This is being seen as a rare victory after the government was forced to withdraw the steel flyover project in 2016 and the recent acquisition of lands in Devanahalli. The Opposition BJP has also claimed credit for the rollback
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru’s civil society groups have welcomed the State Cabinet’s decision on Thursday to withdraw the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allowed for alienation of 5% park land to accommodate the tunnel road project, as a “victory for civic activism and the true essence of democracy.”
This is being seen as a rare victory after the government was forced to withdraw the steel flyover project in 2016 and the recent acquisition of lands in Devanahalli. The Opposition BJP has also claimed credit for the same.
Wider debate
However, with the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister clarifying that the Bill will be put for wider public debate and reintroduced with suitable amendments, civic groups are cautious about how the government would take it forward.
Meanwhile, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly R. Ashok has said that this is a victory for the BJP, the second after the party forced resignation of former Minister B. Nagendra. “The government has announced withdrawal of the Bill within 24 hours of the BJP announcing its protest,” he said. He said that the BJP would oppose taking over park land in future too.
After the Bill was passed without debate in the recently-concluded monsoon session, amid protests by the BJP seeking resignation of Mr. Nagendra, several civic groups had objected to it. This was followed by an online petition against the amendment, which gathered over 25,000 signatures, and subsequent silent demonstrations at Lalbagh.
Greenpeace India, along with several other organisations, first ran a poster campaign under the banner “Not 5%, Not One Inch. Leave Our Parks Alone.” This was followed by a protest walk at Lalbagh on August 30, called by Bengaluru South BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, seeing a large turnout.
N.S. Mukunda, founding member of Bengaluru Praja Vedike, said that when the public presents clear facts and figures in opposition to something, it has to be heard, which is the true essence of democracy. “Bengaluru’s civic activism and participation may have declined over the years, but it remains strong, and mobilisation must improve,” he added.
Environmentalist A.N. Yellappa Reddy, who was at the forefront of opposition to the Bill, said this was a lesson for bureaucrats, technocrats, and government advisors, who should be attentive to public opinion and act in citizens’ interest.
Demand for tunnel project to be scrapped
Following the victory over the Parks Bill, civic groups have now stepped up their demand and called for the controversial tunnel road project to also be scrapped. “The tunnel road projects - both short tunnel and the North-South and East-West Corridors - need to be scrapped. Our fight will continue on that front,” Mr. Mukunda said.
Mr. Surya said the fight was not over yet. “Until the disastrous tunnel road project is officially dropped, neither Lalbagh nor the ancient Peninsular Gneiss Rock is safe,” he said.

stories.headline: In Bengaluru, new civic setup fails to unlock new revenue avenues
stories.bodyText:
A problem that arose when the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) was split into five corporations was the disparity in their revenue capacities, which had to be addressed. However, the new setup will step into another year with revenue capacities largely unchanged.
The Brand Bengaluru Committee had estimated that the North and West corporations would have the lowest property tax collections — ₹543 crore and ₹580 crore, respectively — which is the primary source of revenue for the corporations. Then Bengaluru Development Minister D.K. Shivakumar had said that the corporations would receive financial aid from the government.
“It will also be an opportunity for the appointed corporation commissioners to explore newer avenues for the civic body going forward,” Mr. Shivakumar had said. However, the corporations have largely failed to create newer revenue avenues, although they have strengthened property tax collection.
The new corporations had high hopes for three major sources: advertisement revenue, premium FAR, and B-Khata to A-Khata conversion. While the B-Khata to A-Khata conversion scheme saw a very poor response, premium FAR and advertisement revenue have picked up, according to corporation commissioners. However, the revenue from both avenues is earmarked for B-SMILE’s big-ticket projects, not benefitting corporations.
Failed to create avenues
The very first budget of the five corporations was expected to reflect efforts to explore novel revenue sources, but all of them largely followed a template.
The corporations had an outlay of over ₹3,500 crore each, with hopes of generating revenue from B-Khata to A-Khata conversion and the paid parking system. The paid parking system saw success in the Central Corporation, which implemented it across 10 roads and even at K.R. Market. However, the rest struggled to attract even a single bidder for its implementation.
Now, the Urban Development Department has stepped in with new GBA parking rules, essentially focused on generating revenue through strict parking permits, but these have attracted public criticism. Even towing operations were seen as a potential revenue source, but the operations are currently witnessing negative cash inflow, according to GBA sources.
B-Khata to A-Khata
With much anticipation, the Karnataka government announced the B-Khata to A-Khata conversion scheme. The government had estimated that six lakh properties would come under the scheme and hoped for substantial revenue. It had set a conversion charge of 5% of the guidance value of the area, which meant the conversion charges ran into lakhs of rupees. In addition, the conversion was only for the plot and not for the buildings constructed on the plot.
Despite months having passed since the announcement, only a meagre 12,000 applications were received, forcing the government to offer a rebate of 60% and reduce the conversion charges to 2% of the guidance value. Despite the rebate, by the end of August, only 80,400 applications had been received, which is only 13.4% of the total properties.
Besides, in what came as a setback, premium FAR and advertisement revenue were mandated to be transferred to B-SMILE. Both avenues were fairly good sources of income, with the capability to generate over ₹200 crore.
For example, the North Corporation collected ₹185 crore from premium FAR, but the entire amount was transferred to the SPV.
Strengthening property tax collection
While the corporations attempted to expand their property tax potential, they could only bring in about 18,000 properties under the tax bracket. For the financial year 2026-27, the five corporations have a combined property tax revenue target of over ₹6,700 crore. By August 22, they had collected ₹3,372.48 crore.
The development is attributed to measures such as bringing several properties under the city’s tax bracket, identifying and collecting tax from defaulters, and pursuing arrears. While this has been a positive outcome, the corporations feel that this will improve further when the staff strength is increased.
On Wednesday, GBA Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao said that several surveys, including the SIR, socio-economic survey, and census duties, had affected efforts to strengthen revenue collection.
At the end of the year, according to the commissioners, the new corporations have performed fairly well financially, although the West Corporation’s problems persist. Besides, the corporations are yet to receive the financial aid from the government recommended by the 15th State Finance Commission, which amounts to over ₹800 crore.
However, by the end of December 2025, the government had released funds thrice for the maintenance of the corporations. A corporation commissioner told The Hindu that the civic bodies would execute civic works first and then send the bills to the government for reimbursement. “Even the budget outlay is derived on the terms that the government funds will be claimed later,” he said.
(This is the fifth in a series of reports evaluating the restructuring of Bengaluru governance with the GBA and five corporations, a year after the reform.)

briefs.headline: Safety first, say cop on proposed 2-wheeler curbs in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: The proposed restrictions on two-wheelers and other vehicles on select high-speed flyovers in Bengaluru are primarily aimed at reducing accidents and improving 
road safety
, joint commissioner (traffic) Karthik Reddy said, citing a series of fatal crashes on Electronics City and Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) flyovers.
Reddy said similar restrictions were already in place on select flyovers in Mumbai and Hyderabad, where two-wheelers, three-wheelers and trucks are barred from using certain stretches. “While two-wheelers are banned to safeguard the motorists themselves, trucks are prohibited to avoid traffic congestion and bottlenecks that repeatedly occur whenever they meet with an accident or break down. The Electronics City and KIA flyovers are designed for fast movement and two-wheelers face higher risks than other commuters,” he said.
Strong crosswinds at certain points on the flyovers could also push two-wheeler riders off their lanes, adding to the risks, Reddy said.
The Electronics City flyover recorded 14 fatal accidents involving two-wheelers in 2025, followed by 12 fatal crashes in the first seven months of 2026. The stretch also saw 32 non-fatal accidents in 2025 and another 28 between Jan and July this year. The KIA flyover recorded five fatal and 38 non-fatal accidents in 2025. 
In the first seven months of 2026 alone, 10 fatal and 32 non-fatal accidents were reported.
The proposed restrictions come amid concerns over the impact on Bengaluru’s large two-wheeler population. According to transport department data, as of June 2026, the city had more than 88 lakh registered two-wheelers and 25.3 lakh cars.

briefs.headline: Man caught recording women during morning jog at Bengaluru lake
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A man was caught for allegedly recording videos of women jogging at Agara Lake near HSR Layout Wednesday morning.
When women were out for their usual jog, one of them noticed a man secretly filming them on his mobile phone and confronted him. The matter soon drew the attention of other people on the premises. Some of them checked his phone and found videos of women, raising suspicion that he had been recording them regularly.
A video that went viral on social media mentioned the man as Golden Kumar, a resident of Sarjapur Road. He is said to have apologised and even fallen at the woman’s feet, seeking forgiveness.
A complaint was filed at HSR Layout police station. An officer said: “The complainants had deleted the videos. We are not sure what kind of videos he had recorded.”
The complaint has been treated as a petition as the woman and others were not insisting on an FIR. The suspect told police that he was recording the landscape and had no bad intentions. He was left with a warning.

briefs.headline: 4-wheeler users back flyover curbs in Bengaluru on safety grounds, raise toll concerns
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Lanes are clearly drawn in the debate over the govt’s move to ban two-wheelers from certain flyovers. While two-wheeler riders have voiced strong opposition to the restrictions, four-wheeler users have backed the move on safety grounds, arguing differences in vehicle speeds and rash riding by bikes could make such corridors risky.
At the same time, the proposal has revived questions over toll collection by all vehicle users. While two-wheelers are exempt from paying toll on some NH stretches, motorists are wondering whether they get the quality of travel they pay for.
TOI spoke to regular car users on the move. They had common complaints: A section of two-wheeler riders engage in performing stunts, they change lanes without giving enough notice, weave in and out of lanes as per their convenience and apply brakes suddenly — a potential risk for all road users. Some said wheelies and rash riding were particularly more during early-morning and late-night hours when vehicle users zip by because of thin traffic volume.
Further, motorists pointed to speed differentials between cars and motorcycles on high-speed corridors such as Electronic City flyover and the route towards Kempegowda International Airport (KIA). They argued that vehicles travelling at widely different speeds can lead to sudden braking and dangerous manoeuvres.
At the same time, several motorists conceded a majority of two-wheeler riders follow traffic rules and restrictions would affect a much larger group because of the actions of a few careless riders.
“Some bikers ride without helmets, perform stunts or misuse the road, but 80% of them are responsible. The section that is dangerous on the roads is small, yet significant because of the risks they might unleash on fellow motorists,” Yeshwanth, a cab driver who regularly drives to KIA, said.
His larger concern was toll collection since toll is a passport to smooth and tension-free driving. “We pay up expecting swift commutes. Most times, it’s a line of vehicles on tolled stretches slowing our speed, partly defeating the purpose behind making a payment. Apart from signal-free travel, there’s nothing to write home about the driving experience,” he added.
Subhanshu Sharma, a regular flyover commuter, said two-wheelers can be dangerous on high-speed corridors. “If riders are disciplined and follow lane rules, the threat potential is minimal,” he added.
Sharma, too, touched upon the toll on highways and said expressway-like corridors were not suited for two-wheelers. “If bikers are, indeed, allowed, then they should pay a toll,” he said.
Shreys S, another commuter, struck a cautious note, arguing that restricting a mode of transport raised questions of access and affordability. “Not everyone can afford a car and this is public infrastructure,” the commuter said, adding higher speeds and unsafe lane-changing seen on Bengaluru roads created a genuine safety concern for two-wheeler riders.
The debate played out on social media too. Several users supported restrictions, citing mixed traffic speeds, narrow lanes and the absence of hard shoulders on long elevated stretches. One user said such flyovers could be scary for two-wheeler riders, while another argued that wide-body vehicles like buses and cars were better suited to the Electronic City corridor.

briefs.headline: BDA completes 1,441 percolation wells in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has completed 1,441 rainwater-harvesting percolation wells across 77 BDA parks and residential premises, with the infrastructure estimated to recharge 184.59 million litres (18.459 crore litres) of rainwater annually.
BDA Chairman N.A. Haris handed over the completed wells to the BDA authorities concerned at a programme held at Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout, 4th Block, on Thursday. The authorities will be responsible for their maintenance and upkeep.
The ‘One Billion Drops (OBD) – Groundwater Recharge through Percolation Wells’ project was implemented by United Way of Bengaluru (UWBe) in collaboration with the BDA between February 2025 and February 2026.
“Bengaluru’s water security depends on how effectively the city conserved and recharged water. Every drop we recharge today strengthens Bengaluru’s tomorrow. The percolation wells would help recharge groundwater and make the city more resilient,” Mr. Haris said.
The project is estimated to benefit around 82,300 people. This will also help reduce surface runoff, support groundwater recharge and contribute to flood mitigation and climate resilience, BDA said.
According to the release, the wells, generally around 12 feet deep, were constructed after geological and GIS-based assessments to identify suitable sites based on recharge potential, runoff patterns, available open space and maintenance feasibility. The structures feature concrete rings, aggregate packing, iron mesh and protective covers.
The BDA also launched GreenBengaluruByBDA.in, a digital platform to monitor greening initiatives, sapling health and maintenance, while also providing volunteering opportunities, educational tours and a platform for citizen queries.

briefs.headline: Personalised passenger service at Bengaluru airport sees around 300-350 daily bookings
briefs.deck: Care by BLR which offers tailored services for travellers like meet and assist, porter and luggage service, valet parking, luxury limousine, arrival lounge access and flower services, was launched at KIA in January 2026.
briefs.bodyText:
Around 300-350 bookings are carried out every day by travellers on the Kempegowda International Airport’s (KIA) Care by BLR, a personalised passenger service brand which offers a suite of premium services to the traveller.
Care by BLR which offers seamless, convenient and tailored services like meet and assist, porter and luggage service, valet parking, luxury limousine, arrival lounge access and flower services to meet individual traveller needs was launched at KIA in January 2026.
“Overall if you look at meet and assist, porter and flower services, we have about 300 to 350 transactions everyday,” said George Bennet Kuruvilla, Executive Director and CEO, Bengaluru Airport Services Limited (BASL).
Round-the-clock service
Operating across the airport’s Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, the services function round-the-clock in alignment with flight schedules and can be booked via the BLR Pulse app, the official BLR Airport website and airport counters, with advance bookings recommended and walk-in availability subject to operational feasibility.
“Across the globe, an airport is judged on efficiency. At KIA, we also want the airport to be judged based on empathy. Along with several other initiatives which we have, we have put together this service (Care by BLR) with a slight premiumisation. Care by BLR is a 360 degrees approach to assist every passenger from the kerbside to the gate and the gate to the kerbside,” said George Bennet Kuruvilla, Executive Director and CEO, BASL.
Limo service

There are also airside limousine facilitation services which enable premium, coordinated movement between aircraft and terminal areas designed for VIP, VVIP, business, celebrity and special-assistance journeys, subject to operational and security requirements.

briefs.headline: Amid intense pushback, Karnataka Cabinet decides to withdraw controversial Parks amendment Bill
briefs.deck: The Bill will be opened for public discussion before being reintroduced again in the next legislature session.
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday (September 3, 2026) decided to withdraw the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, that allowed alienation of upto 5% of park and garden land for public infrastructure. It will be opened for public discussion before being reintroduced again in the next legislature session.
The Governor will be intimated about the decision. The bill had been passed in Monsoon Session without discussion amid Opposition’s protest demanding B. Nagendra’s resignation.
The Bill had seen widespread protests by environmental groups, civil society organisations as well as the Opposition BJP leaders. Thousands of citizens had gathered in protest at Lalbagh on August 30 against the amendment Bill which, they argued, aims to facilitate the tunnel road project to take over an acre of Lalbagh land.
Following intense pressure, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had said on September 1, that the proposal could be reviewed and discussed again in the Karnataka Legislature Assembly.
Special legislature session from September 21
In another key decision, the Cabinet decided to hold a three-day special session of Karnataka Legislature from September 21 in the light of farmers’ distress due to severe drought. Detailed discussion on the plight of farmers and impact on public will take place in the session. Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats will also be discussed in detail.
Dept for foreign investments
Among other decisions, Karnataka is set to have a new Department of Global Investment and Overseas Affairs to handle foreign delegations that come with investment proposals. An identity card will be issued to Kannadiga NRIs. Initially, it will be headed by the Chief Minister. The Cabinet also firmed up dates of Invest Karnataka — from April 20 to April 23, 2027 — to attract investments from global investors .

briefs.headline: Bangalore Children’s Chorus to present Don’t Stop Me Now, a concert
briefs.deck: The Bangalore Children’s Chorus will present Don’t Stop Me Now, a musical showcase at Sabha, on September 5 and 6
briefs.bodyText:
“Tonight, I’m gonna have myself a real good time. . .” go the lyrics of ‘Don’t Stop Me Now’ by Queen. “Basically, that underlines what our performers are trying to say with this concert: we are on a ride showcasing, showing off, singing, and enjoying ourselves with this performance,” says Maya Mascarenhas, founder and director of The Bangalore Children’s Chorus.
Directed by Maya and Judith Roby Bidapa, Don’t Stop Me Now will span a wide range of musical genres including jazz, rock, pop and classical music. And in keeping with every performance by the Bangalore Children’s Chorus, the procceds from this show too, will go towards supporting children in need.
According to Maya, the Bangalore Children’s Chorus presents a show every few months. “However, with Don’t Stop Me Now we have tried a different format. We are a 130-strong group comprising 110 children and 20 adults, so this time instead of involving everyone, we have split them in two.”
Though everyone in the group is involved with every production, Maya felt choosing a smaller group this time would give all the members a chance to try out a different role. “Instead of featuring everyone and giving them all a few lines each, this time round, the production will see the efforts of a fewer members playing a bigger role.”
To this end, the Bangalore Children’s Chorus will perform at Sabha, a compact space with limited seating, she says. While Don’t Stop Me Now, will see senior members of the Chorus performing, Maya says the juniors will get their turn under the stagelights at an upcoming show in November.
“This is the first in the series of smaller shows planned for this year, and we are all quite excited to present this new format. We particularly didn’t want to compromise on the quality of our presentation.”
“Our original objective was to identify those with similar talents and give them an opportunity to perform in public. At the same time, we wanted to help them hone their skills in singing, musical theatre, choreography and other areas. Above all, our philosophy has always been ‘children for children’, and that is why any money raised goes to organisations supporting vulnerable children.”
And though this concert will present a mixed bag of genres, including Latin American jazz tunes, rock and pop, that will not only showcase the children’s vocal prowess but also have audiences swaying to the music, Maya says certain classical segments of the evening will require a quieter, reflective approach.
Don’t Stop Me Now by the Bangalore Children’s Chorus will be presented at Sabha on September 5 and September 6, at 4:30pm and 7:30pm on both days. For tickets priced at ₹750 contact 9886045557

stories.headline: Adobe names Anil Chakravarthy as CEO, Narayen transitions to executive chair
stories.deck: Anil Chakravarthy was previously the chief executive of cloud data management company ‌Informatica for four years; ‌Shantanu Narayen has served as CEO for over 18 ‌years
stories.bodyText:
Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy as successor to long-time CEO Shantanu Narayen on Thursday (September 3, 2026), charging the insider with taking on a wave of new AI rivals threatening its design software dominance.
Mr. Narayen, who has served as CEO for over 18 years, will transition to executive chair, the company said.
Adobe has been trying to reassure investors worried about disruptions to its business from potential improvements in AI technology. Its shares have fallen around 18% this year after declining over 21% in 2025.
The Photoshop maker had raised its annual profit forecast in June, reflecting growing demand for its AI products and tools that are central to its strategy to hold on to its lead over challengers like Figma and Canva.
But the firm also announced the exit of finance chief Dan Durn the same month, adding to uncertainties till a permanent successor is named.
It had said in March that Mr. Narayen would step down as CEO once a successor was named, ending a tenure in which he helped turn flagship products such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro and InDesign into household names among creatives worldwide.
Mr. Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 to lead its digital experience business and later took on responsibility for improving how customers interact with Adobe, as well as overseeing its global sales and customer-support teams.

stories.headline: Sebi to tweak CAS, change method for derivative trade
stories.deck: Consultation Paper On Settlement Prices Within A Week
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Thursday said it will revise the settlement price mechanism for derivatives contracts for Closing Auction Session (CAS). The decision comes exactly a month after CAS was rolled out on Aug 3. Sebi will soon come out with a consultation paper for revising the mechanism, a release from the regulator said.
During the past month, introduction of CAS created significant market volatility and at times led to closing price discrepancies between two exchanges. In contrast, globally, CAS is used for a better closing price discovery. Sebi had shifted to CAS from the earlier system of Volume-weighted Average Price (V-WAP) for all stocks traded in the derivatives segment.
Over the past month, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had reiterated on at least two occasions that the regulator would not change the CAS process but was willing to tweak it after looking into trading data.On Aug 20, Sebi had penalised Copthall, a JP Morgan entity registered as an FPI in India, and Mansi Broking, a domestic broker, for manipulating sensex levels during CAS on Aug 13, a weekly F&O contracts expiry day.
 Then again Aug 27, a day for monthly F&O contracts expiry, there was huge price volatility in sensex and banked contracts during CAS. On Thursday also sensex saw some sharp volatility during CAS.
"The framework for CAS was introduced following extensive stakeholder consultations and detailed policy deliberations," the Sebi release said. "Since its implementation, Sebi has closely engaged with various stakeholders, including stock exchanges, brokers, proprietary traders, software vendors, mutual funds, industry associations and FPIs, with a view to facilitating smooth implementation and addressing operational and other issues arising during the initial period of adoption."
The release said that the regulator had been closely monitoring the functioning of CAS and its impact on the market during the first month of its operation. "During this period, Sebi has received feedback and suggestions from various market participants and stakeholders through multiple channels, including social media and other media platforms. Among the issues raised, a significant area of feedback relates to the determination of settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry based on the closing pr ice determined through CAS."

stories.headline: Govt eyes auto cos-led model to fix EV charging on highways
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt wants automakers to take greater responsibility for fixing gaps in India's electric vehicle EV charging network. Speaking at Siam's annual session, Kamran Rizvi, secretary, ministry of heavy industries, said nearly half of mapped charging stations were non-functional, underscoring a major consumer pain point as EV adoption expands.
The ministry has identified 60 priority corridors for electrification and has shared the list with Siam. Rizvi suggested the industry body could coordinate with automakers to divide these stretches among OEMs (original equipment manufacturers), which would then work towards deploying charging infrastructure on their assigned highways.
"We should be able to saturate all the important highways in the next two to three years," he said.
The proposal comes as govt gradually reduces direct subsidies for EV purchases and looks to industry to shoulder a larger part of the ecosystem build-out. Rizvi pointed to electric three-wheelers, where penetration has reached around 50%, as evidence that some segments can continue growing without perpetual subsidy support.
The heavy industries ministry also has a Rs 2,000 crore corpus for charging infrastructure, which Rizvi said could be extended to automakers for deployment. 
Charging depots are also planned across 160 cities to support the electrification of buses.
Rizvi said charging should be easier to scale than conventional fuel retailing because it does not require the same upstream supply chain. "Charging is a standalone business," he said, urging automakers to play a more direct role not just in installing chargers, but also in ensuring they remain functional and dependable for consumers.

briefs.headline: Nvidia’s price hike plan may raise India’s AI infra costs
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India’s AI infrastructure push could get more expensive. Nvidia’s reported plan to raise AI server prices by around 15% from next year is expected to increase deployment costs for GPU cloud providers, data-centre operators and companies building large compute clusters, with industry executives warning that some of the increase may ultimately be passed on to customers.
The impact could be particularly significant as India scales up AI compute capacity across private data centres, cloud platforms and govt-backed programmes. Higher hardware costs could force operators to reassess expansion plans, delay fresh capacity additions or explore alternative chip architectures.
“Nvidia’s pricing is driven largely by demand and component costs, especially memory, which remains tight and is projected to rise through 2027,” said Ishan Talathi, founder and CEO of CloudPe. Talathi said Nvidia had already raised prices of its RTX Pro 6000 series from $13,250 to $16,000 earlier this month, an increase of 20.8% in two months.
“For an AI cloud platform like CloudPe, where GPU servers are among the biggest capex items, this translates into a 10-12% increase in overall deployment costs,” he said. CloudPe expects GPU cloud pricing in India to rise by 10-15% over the next 12-18 months unless memory supply improves or alternative architectures gain traction.
And, the pressure is not restricted to GPUs. Amit Chaurasia, data infrastructure expert and founder of Dataneers, said sharp increases in prices of memory and storage components were already affecting enterprise buying decisions.
“It’s not GPUs but HDDs and RAMs that have quadrupled in price. This is an unprecedented rise,” Chaurasia said, adding that customers were delaying purchases in the hope that prices would ease. While large enterprises may have the financial capacity to absorb higher costs, smaller companies could be more vulnerable. Chaurasia said SMEs were more likely to defer technology investments, while higher hardware costs could have a cascading effect across sectors as technology becomes an increasingly important input for businesses.

briefs.headline: EV shift puts auto parts MSMEs under pressure
briefs.bodyText:
CHENNAI: India's shift towards electric mobility and tech-intensive vehicles is exposing a capability gap among auto component manufacturers, particularly MSMEs, even as imports of batteries, power electronics, embedded software and advanced electronics rise.
Domestic OEM sourcing of auto components grew 16% to Rs 6.6 lakh crore in FY26, while component exports reached Rs 2.1 lakh crore. But imports are growing faster, with China accounting for about 36% of India's auto component imports, according to a study by Vector Consulting Group.
The challenge is significant for MSMEs, which account for around 80% of India's auto parts producers. While advanced engineering, electronics, embedded software and systems integration are increasingly critical to competitiveness, fewer than half of MSME suppliers are estimated to have these capabilities. Embedded software capability exists in only about 10% of suppliers and systems integration and product development capabilities in around 14%.
"India's automotive opportunity will depend on how quickly capability can be built across the supplier ecosystem," Ravindra Patki, Managing Partner, Vector Consulting Group, told TOI. "Policy support has an important role in creating the right environment, but it cannot by itself close the capability gap."
The financial constraints of smaller suppliers make the transition harder. Inventory levels can reach 60 days in some cases, locking up working capital, while EBITDA margins remain around 12%. Only about 10% of suppliers are estimated to have the financial capacity to invest consistently in technology, engineering and product development.

briefs.headline: Volkswagen says cutting 100,000 jobs by end of decade
briefs.deck: The firm had approved a plan which involved "the reduction of around 50,000 jobs", on top of another 50,000 already agreed, Volkswagen said in a statement
briefs.bodyText:
German car giant Volkswagen said on Thursday (September 3, 2026) that management and unions had agreed to cut a further 50,000 jobs by the end of the decade, bringing total job losses to 100,000.
"It is essential to systematically align workforce levels with economic realities," the 10-brand group said in a statement.
The firm had approved a plan which involved "the reduction of around 50,000 jobs", on top of another 50,000 already agreed, it added.
Hit by U.S. tariffs, patchy demand for electric cars and above all fierce competition in and from China, Europe's largest carmaker is in trouble.
The firm, which apart from its namesake also includes brands such as Audi and Porsche, had already agreed to cut about 50,000 jobs worldwide.
The total 100,000 cuts will be the largest restructuring ever carried out in the global automotive industry, amounting to about 15% of the carmaker's staff worldwide.
Volkswagen further said that both management and unions agreed that the future of four German plants — in Hannover, Emden, Zwickau and Neckarsulm — could not be assured into the 2030s.
The plants closing would mark the first time Volkswagen had shuttered full-scale factories in its home country.
The adoption of the plans by Volkswagen's supervisory board, made up of both labour and shareholder representatives, marks progress in delicate negotiations between the two sides.
"The supervisory board has unanimously approved the executive board's future plan presented today," CEO Oliver Blume said. "This is a strong signal for the future of the Volkswagen Group."

briefs.headline: Automakers optimistic about festive demand
briefs.deck: Citing the Wagon R as an example, he said the model recorded 21,000 registrations, which is a level last seen five to six years ago and underscored the impact of GST 2.0.
briefs.bodyText:
India’s automobile industry is expected to grow by 10% this fiscal year and is optimistic about the upcoming festive season, with Onam already off to a positive start.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court disposes of SEBI appeals against NSE in co-location, dark fibre cases
briefs.deck: In July, SEBI had accepted two settlement applications filed by the NSE for an aggregate amount of about ₹1,492 crore. Of this, about ₹1,224 crore pertained to the co-location case, while ₹268 crore related to the dark fibre case, also known as the leased-line connectivity case.
briefs.bodyText:
The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 3, 2026) disposed of a batch of appeals filed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) against the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in the co-location and dark fibre cases, following a settlement of nearly ₹1,500 crore between the market regulator and the exchange.
A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran was hearing SEBI’s appeals against orders of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) setting aside disgorgement directions issued by the regulator against the NSE in the two cases. The Bench disposed of the appeals after taking note of the settlement between the parties.
In July, SEBI had accepted two settlement applications filed by the NSE for an aggregate amount of about ₹1,492 crore. Of this, about ₹1,224 crore pertained to the co-location case, while ₹268 crore related to the dark fibre case, also known as the leased-line connectivity case.
The cases stem from allegations that certain brokers were given preferential access to the NSE’s trading systems through its co-location facility, potentially allowing them to receive market data ahead of others. The allegations of unfair access first surfaced following a whistle-blower complaint in January 2015.
Co-location allows brokers to place their computer servers at an exchange’s data centre, reducing the time taken to receive market data and execute trades. Dark fibre refers to dedicated optical fibre connectivity that can facilitate faster transmission of data between two point.
In the main co-location case, SEBI had in 2019 directed the NSE to disgorge ₹625 crore, along with 12% annual interest from April 1, 2014. The regulator had alleged that the exchange provided preferential connectivity to select brokers accessing its tick-by-tick data dissemination servers, giving them an advantage over other market participants.
The NSE challenged the order before the SAT, which subsequently set aside SEBI’s disgorgement direction. The market regulator then approached the apex court against the appellate tribunal’s ruling.
In a separate order in 2019, SEBI directed the NSE to disgorge ₹62.6 crore, along with 12% annual interest from September 11, 2015, in the dark fibre case.
The regulator had alleged that the NSE gave preferential treatment to two brokers by allowing them to use the services of an unlicensed telecom vendor to establish point-to-point connectivity between their co-location racks at the NSE and the BSE.
SAT subsequently quashed the disgorgement direction in this case as well, prompting SEBI to challenge the ruling before the Supreme Court.
The two appeals have now been disposed of following the settlement between SEBI and the NSE.
The settlement comes as the country’s largest stock exchange prepares for its stock-market debut, nearly a decade after it first sought to list its shares, with its plans having faced prolonged regulatory hurdles. The proposed initial public offering (IPO) is expected to raise around ₹30,000 crore, which would make it one of the largest IPOs in India’s capital market history.

stories.headline: ‘I didn’t know all of this happened’: Mandhana reacts after rewriting history
stories.deck: Smriti Mandhana set a new record by scoring 124 runs in an impressive innings against Hong Kong, playing a pivotal role in India's decisive victory in the tournament. This milestone marks her as the first Indian woman to reach this T20 international achievement, surpassing Mithali Raj in total runs. Next up, India is poised to challenge Pakistan in a much-anticipated match.
stories.bodyText:
Smriti Mandhana
 produced a record-breaking knock as India stormed into the Women's Asia Cup semi-final with a 137-run win over Hong Kong on Thursday. The India opener smashed 124 off 64 balls, helping her side post 193 for five before Hong Kong were bowled out for 56 in 16.2 overs.
Mandhana
's century was her second in T20 internationals and made her the only Indian woman to achieve the feat. She also moved past 
Meg Lanning
 for the most international centuries in women's cricket, reaching 18 hundreds across formats. Later in the innings, she surpassed Mithali Raj to become the leading run-scorer in women's internationals.
Despite the historic nature of her innings, Mandhana admitted she was unaware of the records she had broken.
"I didn't know all of this happened," Mandhana said after being informed about her record-breaking effort.
Asked who she would dedicate the century to, the Player of the Match said her family remained closest to her heart.
"I don't have anyone in mind who I would like to dedicate, but definitely, my family."
Mandhana also explained how she approached the Hong Kong attack, having never faced the opposition before.
"We’re not really aware of (the opposition). We had seen a few videos, but not really aware. 
We’re playing them for the first time, so when you come against a bowler who you don’t know a lot, you have to just forget that you’ve played whatever cricket. You just have to go, watch the ball, and I think it was more about just adjusting to the pace."
The left-hander initially took some time to settle before accelerating alongside Shafali Verma, who scored 28 off 17 balls. Mandhana eventually struck seven sixes and 14 boundaries, making batting look effortless despite the surface not being particularly easy for strokeplay.
She was also asked about missing out on some full tosses during the powerplay and admitted that such deliveries are not necessarily her strength.
"I would say that full tosses are not my strength (laughs). I’m happy that I could get away with a few of the full tosses today. I think any top-order batter would say that sometimes full tosses can go for a six, or you can get out."
Mandhana had earlier acknowledged Hong Kong's disciplined bowling, particularly during the powerplay.
"It's really hard for me to play slower bowlers, but credit to them. They were really disciplined in the powerplay. They bowled pretty well, and the kind of energy they showed was something which we all can learn from. Having said that, I just love batting, and I'm happy that I could contribute."
India secured their second win in as many matches and will face Pakistan on Saturday.

stories.headline: Smriti Mandhana surpasses Mithali Raj as women’s international cricket’s leading run-scorer
stories.deck: During India’s Asia Cup match against Hong Kong in Dubai, she went past Mithali Raj, the woman who almost single-handedly put Indian women’s cricket in the headlines when the sport had no takers, to become the leading scorer of international runs.
stories.bodyText:
On that warm afternoon in Jaipur, Smriti Mandhana was talking about her childhood, about how her mother instilled a sense of competitiveness in her.
Also Read | Style and substance: Smriti Mandhana’s batting is eye-catching and effective
“She always used to ask me to persevere, in whatever I did, and not to leave in the middle but to go on till reaching the top,” Smriti told The Hindu. She also said she wanted to be the best batter in the world.
She already was. And that was seven years ago.
Former New Zealand all-rounder Scott Styris even said, around that time, the difference between Smriti and the next batter in women’s cricket was the size of Mumbai.
When one asked her if she was aware of that remark by Styris, she said she wasn’t, but she was happy, and smiled. The smile that cricket fans across the world have become so used to.
Sweet certainly that smile is, but her batting is sweeter.
Not many cricketers, male or female, have made batting such a fine art. She is a treat to watch. Like David Gower or Sourav Ganguly was.
Runs continue to flow from her bat. As do records. There were more of them on Thursday (September 3, 2026).
During India’s Asia Cup match against Hong Kong in Dubai, she went past Mithali Raj, the woman who almost single-handedly put Indian women’s cricket in the headlines when the sport had no takers, to become the leading scorer of international runs. She overtook Mithali’s tally 10,868 runs during her innings of 124 off 64 balls against Hong Kong.
And that was her 18th hundred. Also a record. She is now the scorer of most international hundreds in women’s cricket; she moved past Meg Lanning, the former Australian captain who hit 17 before she quit international cricket at the age of 31, and South Africa captain Laura Wolvaardt, who has an equal number of centuries.
Smriti is only 30. She should be around for many more years. She will remain driven to be the best.
