stories.headline: Asia Cup: India storm into semis as Mandhana’s record 124, spin blitz crush Hong Kong
stories.deck: In a stunning display of skill, Smriti Mandhana smashed 124 runs, leading India to an impressive total. The bowlers followed suit, limiting Hong Kong to just 56 runs. This commanding 137-run victory not only showcased India's strength but also secured their entry into the Women's Asia Cup semi-finals, with Mandhana setting new records in women's international cricket.
stories.bodyText:
Smriti Mandhana's record-breaking 124 and a clinical bowling effort helped India crush Hong Kong by 137 runs in their Women's Asia Cup 2026 clash in Dubai. After posting 193/5, India bowled Hong Kong out for just 56 in 16.2 overs to seal a massive win and book their place in the semi-finals.
Mandhana’s record-breaking assault
Hong Kong won the toss and elected to field, but Mandhana quickly put their decision under pressure. The India opener and Shafali Verma gave their side a strong start, with Verma smashing 28 off 17 balls before departing.
Wickets began to fall regularly after the opening stand, but Mandhana continued to attack from one end. She reached her half-century in 40 balls before dramatically increasing the tempo, bringing up her century in just 57 deliveries.
Mandhana finished with a sensational 124 off 64 balls, hitting 14 fours and seven sixes at a strike rate of 193.75. The innings took her to 18 international centuries, moving her past Meg Lanning's tally of 17 and making her the leading century-maker in women's international cricket.
She also broke Chamari Athapaththu's record for the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing the Sri Lankan's unbeaten 119.
Mandhana's innings eventually ended in the final over when she was run out after a mix-up with Bharti Fulmali. Her dismissal, however, came after she had already powered India to a formidable 193/5.
India’s spinners choke Hong Kong
Hong Kong's chase never got going as India's spin-heavy attack strangled the batting lineup from the beginning. They slipped to 32/3 and struggled to score freely against India's disciplined bowling.
Deepti Sharma led the attack with 3/9 from three overs, removing key batters Natasha Miles and Yasmin Daswani while keeping the scoring rate under control. Prema Rawat, Nandani Sharma and Shree Charani then continued to chip away at the Hong Kong batting order.
Marina Lamplough offered some resistance with 14, but Shree Charani eventually removed her before the lower order folded quickly. Nandani Sharma claimed two wickets, while Prema Rawat finished with two as India's spinners kept the pressure on.
Hong Kong were eventually bowled out for just 56 in 16.2 overs. Shree Charani completed the victory by stumping Shanzeen Shahzad after a sharp piece of work from Richa Ghosh.

briefs.headline: Indian hockey teams set for double title defence as Junior Asia Cup begins in China

briefs.bodyText:
The Indian under-21 men's hockey team will eye a record-extending sixth title, while the women will chase a hat-trick of trophies when the defending champions in both categories begin their AHF Junior Asia Cup campaigns here on Friday.
The women's team, which lifted the Asia Cup trophy in the last two editions, will be led by mid-fielder Khaidem Shileima Chanu this time.
The team has undergone a structured training programme under coach Tim White, who assumed charge earlier this year.
As part of their preparations, an extended squad undertook an exposure tour of the United Kingdom, where they played matches against Scotland Senior Women, USA U-21, England U-21 and Belgium U-21.
India, placed in the Elite Pool, will begin their campaign against South Korea on September 5. The team will then face Malaysia on September 6, before taking on Japan on September 8 and hosts China on September 9.
"Our first game is against South Korea on Saturday, so we are preparing for that. The team has acclimatized well. The weather is a bit cooler (in Moqi), but conditions are good and we are really looking forward to Match 1," said White in a press release issued by Hockey India.
"In terms of our expectations, we prepared well in Bengaluru over a number of months, including a tour of the UK and some games against a combined team.
"We feel our game is in good order and we are well prepared to play against the best teams in Asia. We are looking forward to seeing how our game plan is going to stand up against the best teams. I am sure the girls will do India proud."
Men's team targets record-extending sixth Trophy
The men's team will also enter the competition with the distinction of having won the continental title five times, including the last three editions.
Defender Anmol Ekka will captain the side, while newly appointed coach Frederic Soyez will look to begin his tenure with a title win.
The squad has undergone extensive preparation, including an exposure tour of Belgium, where the team competed against strong international U-21 opposition from Austria, Belgium, Germany and the Netherlands.
The team also played a series of friendly games at home against the Malaysian U-21 side in Bengaluru, followed by a three-match series against hosts China in Dalian.
"Our progression has been quite good. The last (friendly) game against China (an 8-2 win for India) was very positive," said coach Soyez.
"It gave our confidence a huge boost heading into the tournament. We spent one week in Dalian, getting used to the conditions in China, before arriving in Moqi ahead of our opening match against Indonesia on Saturday.
"Our main expectation from this tournament is to keep progressing and become more confident and consistent, maintain solid defensive structure and raise our level of performance with every match," Soyez added.

briefs.headline: M. Siddharth embraces PowerPlay challenge after starring in Kovai Kings’ TNPL title run

briefs.bodyText:
There is something revealing in the way M. Siddharth talks about bowling in the PowerPlay. It is not merely a job he has been given, or a tactical responsibility. He describes it as a challenge.
“It’s obviously very challenging. I want to do it because it’s a challenge. If I do well, then it’s good for the team. Why am I being preferred over a fast bowler to bowl with the new ball? If a fast bowler is going to give two overs for 20, then I should be able to do better than that. If I can give two overs for 10 or 12, and even take a wicket, that’s an impact for me,” he said over the phone on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).
Siddharth was central to Vida Kovai Kings’ latest TNPL title run, finishing second on the wickets chart with 16 wickets and recording the tournament’s best economy rate (5.08). Ten of his wickets came in the PowerPlay. He also regularly bowled arm-balls above 110 kph.
“I have always felt that’s a wicket-taking delivery for me. I see that as a strength,” he said.
He played only four IPL games this season, but said he “was able to bring that confidence and learnings into the TNPL.”
He’s worked with Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) spin-bowling coach Carl Crowe, who helped remodel Sunil Narine’s action. “We worked a lot on my technique and variations like backspinner, carrom ball, bouncer, and yorker. He gave me a lot of confidence. I was able to explore more of my bowling,” Siddharth said.
The bouncer was worked on extensively after Krunal Pandya’s use of it gave Siddharth the confidence to try it himself.
“After watching him bowl that, I felt I could do it as well - that I was capable of it. I bowled it a lot in IPL practice. It came out well,” he said. He even brought out that bouncer in this TNPL.

briefs.headline: Srikanth stuns Lai, Tanvi loses in China Masters, Satwik-Chirag too win
briefs.deck: The 33-year-old Srikanth, who had reached the US Open Super 300 final earlier this year, rallied his way to notch up an upset 21-18 21-19 win over Lai, who won his second World Championships bronze in New Delhi last month.
briefs.bodyText:
Veteran Indian shuttler Kidambi Srikanth stunned world No. 9 Victor Lai of Canada in straight games to enter the men's singles quarterfinals of the China Masters Super 750 badminton tournament here on Thursday.
The 33-year-old Srikanth, who had reached the U.S. Open Super 300 final earlier this year, rallied his way to notch up an upset 21-18 21-19 win over Lai, who won his second World Championships bronze in New Delhi last month.
"I wasn't really thinking about the score. I was only thinking about what I have been doing throughout the match and what I need to do going forward, that's the only thing I was thinking about," Srikanth said.
"He has been playing really well for last 12-14 months but I just feel like it is a new day and if I can play my best, I will have my chances. I wasn't thinking about how he has been playing. I was only thinking about how I should play." A former world No. 1 and 2021 World Championships silver-medallist, Srikanth will face Hong Kong's Lee Cheuk Yiu in his next match.
Men's doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty overcame a mid-match wobble to beat French brothers Christo and Toma Junior Popov 21-15 22-24 21-9 and progress to the quarterfinals.
In women's singles, Tanvi Sharma, who won the Taipei Open World Tour Super 300 title recently, showed gumption to fight but imploded at the back end to go down 17-21 21-18 16-21 to world No. 9 Tomoka Miyazaki of Japan in the second round.
India's Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also bowed out after losing 18-21 18-21 to Chinese Taipei's Liu Kuang Heng and Hsu Yin Hui in mixed doubles.
Srikanth vs Lai
Srikanth showed his ability to fight and rained down thunderous jump smashes to telling effect.
After an initial 3-3 start, Srikanth fell behind 3-7 but recovered to 8-8 as Lai committed a series of unforced errors.
The Canadian, who won his maiden Super 1000 title in Indonesia this year, went into the interval with a two-point cushion.
Lai seemed to find his rhythm as he cramped Srikanth with his smashes to move to 15-11.
However, the veteran Indian pushed one to the backline, followed it up with a jump-smash winner and then outwitted his rival at the net. Lai sprayed one into the net as it became 15-15.
Another cross-court smash took the Indian to 18-16. Srikanth soon grabbed three game points with a net shot and sealed it on his second chance when Lai found the net again.
After the change of sides, Srikanth was again lagging but kept breathing down his rival's neck.
Srikanth fell 5-9 behind after a series of unforced errors.
Left to do the catching up act again, Srikanth kept fighting. From 9-14, two smashes from Srikanth and a couple of net errors from his rival helped the Indian make it 13-14. An attacking cross-court return made it 14-15 as Srikanth kept snapping at his rival's feet.
He soon clawed back to 18-18. Lai then went long and Srikanth sent one into the forehand corner to earn match points. The Canadian sprayed wide again as Srikanth pumped his fist after sealing the win.
Satwit-Chirag vs Popov brothers
The Indians were in control from the outset, taking an 11-6 lead at the interval in the opening game. There were hardly any long rallies as Satwik and Chirag kept the exchanges tight.
The French pair struggled against the Indians' interceptions and angled returns, with the Popovs repeatedly offering loose lifts that were punished. Satwik and Chirag surged to 18-11 before a return to Toma Junior's hip area left him cramped and earned the Indians seven game points. They eventually sealed the opener with a fortunate net cord.
The second game was far more competitive, with the Popovs leading 11-10 at the interval. The Indians moved ahead 18-15, but a wide lift from Satwik and a moment of confusion allowed the French duo to level at 18-18.
The Popov brothers saved two match points before earning a game point at 23-22 and forcing a decider when Chirag's return found the net.
Satwik and Chirag responded strongly, racing to a 6-1 lead and taking an 11-5 advantage at the interval. They never looked back, winning a superb 33-shot rally to move to 15-6 before closing out the match comfortably.

briefs.headline: KCL | Vignesh’s five-for helps Globstars edge Royals and enter the last four; Vishnu’s brilliant ton in vain
briefs.bodyText:
T20 is a game of fine margins and Calicut Globstars tried its best to test that theory at the Sports Hub Greenfield stadium on Thursday!
Globstars dropped six chances, including four from centurion Vishnu Vinod, yet held its nerve to eke out a seven-run win over Trivandrum Royals to move into the semifinals of the Kerala Cricket League.
Leg-spinner Vignesh Puthur with the season’s first five wicket haul (five for 13) was the standout performer for Globstar and the lone bowler not to receive the punishment from Vishnu who battled as a one-man army for Royals.
Vishnu blasted a blazing century (118, 62b, 10x4, 8x6) making full use of the reprieves to keep his side in the hunt. However, his luck ran out when he top-edged a pull from Akhil Scaria and Rohan Kunnummal covered sufficient ground from long-off to complete the catch at mid off.
Chasing 185, Royals were in control when Vishnu Vinod and Krishna Prasad added 51-runs for the second wicket. But the introduction of Vignesh in the 10th over changed the contest. He dismissed Krishna Prasad (14), slogging a catch to Akhil Scaria at long on and had Govind Dev Pai (0) stumped.
Vignesh’s two more wickets — Sijomon Joseph (2) and M. Nikhil (0) — in the 14th over swung the match in favour of Globstar as Royals slumped to 97 for six.
But Vishnu refused to give up and took 19 runs from the 16th over bowled by M.U. Harikrishnan. He clattered three sixes and slogged Akhin Sathar over midwicket for a boundary to reach his hundred from 56 balls. However, Scaria came back to dismiss Vishnu and with it ended Royals’ hopes.
Earlier, lower order contributions from Salman Nizar (31 not out) and Aswin Anand (24 not out) helped Globstars post 184 for six.

briefs.headline: Smriti Mandhana equals Mithali Raj’s big record, then creates more history
briefs.deck: Smriti Mandhana achieved a significant milestone by equaling Mithali Raj's record for fifty-plus scores. She reached this landmark during India's Women's Asia Cup match against Hong Kong China. Mandhana then transitioned to an exceptional T20I century, scoring 124 runs off 64 balls. This remarkable innings also set a new record for the highest individual score in the Women's T20 Asia Cup.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Smriti Mandhana
 added another major milestone to her already glittering international career on Thursday, equalling 
Mithali Raj
's record for the most 50-plus scores in women's international cricket during India's Women's Asia Cup clash against Hong Kong China in Dubai.
Mandhana brought up her half-century off 40 balls, reaching the landmark in style by smashing Iqra Sahar over deep backward square-leg for a six. It was her 93rd 50-plus score in women's international cricket, taking her level with India's legendary former captain Mithali Raj at the top of the list.
The milestone came during an innings in which Mandhana went on to produce one of the most extraordinary T20I performances of her career.
Mithali, who retired from international cricket in 2022, had held the record outright with 93 scores of 50 or more across formats. Mandhana's latest half-century finally brought her alongside the Indian batting great.
England's Charlotte Edwards is third on the list with 80 50-plus scores, followed by New Zealand's Suzie Bates on 79 and West Indies great Stafanie Taylor and South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt on 74 each.
Most 50-plus scores in women’s international cricket
- 93 - Mithali Raj
- 93 - Smriti Mandhana
- 80 - Charlotte Edwards
- 79 - Suzie Bates
- 74 -Stafanie Taylor
- 74 - Laura Wolvaardt
Mandhana matches Mithali, then shifts gears
Having equalled Mithali's landmark, Mandhana transformed her innings from controlled aggression into an astonishing assault.
The left-hander took just 17 deliveries to move from 50 to 100, completing her second T20I century in only 57 balls.
In the process, Mandhana became the first Indian woman to score two T20I centuries. Her first had come against England at Trent Bridge in 2025, when she made 112.
Her latest hundred also took her tally to 18 centuries in women's international cricket, moving her ahead of Meg Lanning and Laura Wolvaardt, who have 17 each.
Mandhana eventually departed in the final over after smashing 124 off 64 balls, with her spectacular innings containing 14 fours and seven sixes.
The knock also became the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history, surpassing Chamari Athapaththu's unbeaten 119 against Malaysia in 2024.
Another record partnership with Shafali
Mandhana's latest landmark also came alongside another record involving her long-time opening partner Shafali Verma.
The pair's 50-plus partnership was their 29th in T20Is, comfortably the most by any pair in the format. UAE's Esha Oza and Theertha Satish are second on the list with 23, while Australia's Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney have 20.
Across formats, Mandhana and Shafali have now registered 44 50-plus partnerships in women's internationals. The next-best pair is New Zealand's Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates, with 37.
Mandhana also strengthened her position at the top of the list for 50-plus scores in women's T20Is, with her latest effort taking her tally to 37. Australia's Beth Mooney is next with 33.

briefs.headline: Smriti Mandhana creates history, surpasses Lanning to become leading century-maker
briefs.deck: In an exhilarating display of skill, Smriti Mandhana shattered records by scoring her 18th international century, amassing 124 runs in just 64 balls. Her explosive knock led India to a formidable total of 193 runs. Shafali Verma played a vital role at the start with her brisk 28, setting the tone for a dominant batting showcase by the Indian team.
briefs.bodyText:
Smriti Mandhana
 produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting to script a new world record as India Women posted a formidable 193/5 against Hong Kong in their Women's Asia Cup 2026 clash in Dubai on Thursday.
Mandhana became the leading century-maker in women's international cricket, moving to 18 centuries and surpassing former Australia captain Meg Lanning's record of 17. South Africa's Laura Wolvaardt also has 17 international hundreds, while Hayley Matthews has 15.
Most 100s in Women's International Cricket
- 18 – Smriti Mandhana
- 17 – Meg Lanning
- 17 – Laura Wolvaardt
- 15 – Hayley Matthews
- 14 – Suzie Bates
- 14 – Tammy Beaumont
Asked to bat first after Hong Kong won the toss, India got off to a flying start with Mandhana and Shafali Verma putting the opposition bowlers under pressure. Verma struck 28 off 17 balls before her dismissal brought Hong Kong back into the contest.
However, Mandhana remained unfazed as wickets continued to tumble at the other end. She reached her half-century from 40 balls but shifted gears dramatically after reaching the landmark, turning the innings into a one-woman assault.
The India vice-captain raced from 50 to 100 in just 17 balls, bringing up her century in only 57 deliveries. 
She continued attacking until the final delivery of the innings, finishing with a spectacular 124 off 64 balls, including 14 fours and seven sixes, at a staggering strike rate of 193.75.
Mandhana's innings also saw her rewrite the record books for the highest individual score in Women's T20 Asia Cup history.
Highest individual scores in Women's T20 Asia Cup
- 124 – Smriti Mandhana (IND-W) vs HKG-W, Dubai, 2026
- 119 – Chamari Athapaththu (SL-W) vs MAS-W, Dambulla, 2024*
- 97 – Mithali Raj (IND-W) vs MAS-W, Kuala Lumpur, 2018*
- 81 – Harshitha Samarawickrama (SL-W) vs THA-W, Sylhet, 2022
- 81 – Shafali Verma (IND-W) vs NEP-W, Dambulla, 2024
Mandhana's innings came to an unfortunate end in the final over. Looking to steal a single after Bharti Fulmali sliced a yorker towards point, Mandhana set off but was never in the frame when the throw came in. Iqra Sahar's direct throw to the striker's end caught her well short, bringing a spectacular innings to a disappointing conclusion.
Despite the late run-out, Mandhana had already done enough damage to put India in a commanding position. Her 124 accounted for nearly two-thirds of India's total and ensured India finished with 193/5 from their 20 overs, leaving Hong Kong a daunting target of 194.
Shafali Verma's 28 off 17 provided India with the early impetus, while Richa Ghosh (11), Harmanpreet Kaur (10) and Deepti Sharma (1*) contributed around Mandhana's record-breaking effort. For Hong Kong, Marina Lamplough was the standout bowler, claiming 2/46, while Joyleen Kaur, Ruchitha Venkatesh and Iqra Sahar picked up one wicket each.

briefs.headline: BCCI breaks silence on Asian Games concerns, promises ‘best facilities’ for Team India
briefs.deck: The BCCI has responded to worries surrounding the accommodation for Indian cricket teams during the Asian Games, with secretary Devajit Saikia assuring that there are no pressing concerns. The board is dedicated to delivering high-quality amenities for both players and staff. Under VVS Laxman’s leadership, the men's team will compete, while Amol Muzumdar coaches the women's team, as India seek to…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The 
Board of Control for Cricket in India
 (BCCI) has moved to allay concerns over accommodation and logistical arrangements for the Indian cricket squads at the upcoming 
Asian Games
 in Aichi-Nagoya, with secretary Devajit Saikia insisting there is no immediate issue but promising that the board will step in if required.
Questions had emerged over the facilities available for participating cricket teams ahead of the multi-sport event in Japan, particularly around accommodation and infrastructure. The Japan Cricket Association (JCA) has said teams have been offered hotel accommodation and are also free to make their own arrangements.
Speaking after Thursday's review meeting at BCCI headquarters in Mumbai, Saikia said the board was confident about India's arrangements and would not hesitate to create its own system if the situation demanded it.
“There is no such issue that we have discussed or which is on our agenda today or prior to today also. So we are not going to have any difficulties in Japan. If any kind of situation arises, we will take an appropriate call at the right time so that we ensure that our players and the support staff will get the best facilities in the Asian Games, whether it is from the organisers.
“If required, BCCI will have its own system in place to provide the best facilities to our players,” Saikia told reporters.
Japan accommodation concerns
The reassurance comes amid wider logistical questions surrounding the Aichi-Nagoya Games. Organisers confirmed last week that accommodation had been secured for all registered athletes and officials despite entries exceeding 17,000, with participants set to be housed across hotels, temporary accommodation and a cruise ship rather than a traditional athletes' village.
For cricket, JCA chief executive officer Naoki Alex Miyaji had sought to ease concerns by saying participating teams were being offered hotel accommodation.
India will enter the Asian Games as defending champions in both men's and women's T20 cricket. The men's side will be led by 
Shreyas Iyer
, while Harmanpreet Kaur will captain the women's side.
Laxman to lead men's side
VVS Laxman, director of cricket at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, will take charge of the men's side in Japan. He will be assisted by Sunil Joshi, Hrishikesh Kanitkar and Subhadeep Ghosh.
Laxman was also in charge when India won the men's gold medal at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou.
Regular head coach Gautam Gambhir will remain with the senior side for the home ODI series against the West Indies, beginning September 27.
The women's side will be coached by Amol Muzumdar, with Aavishkar Salvi and Munish Bali assisting him.
India's men's campaign will begin on September 24, while the women's side will enter at the quarterfinal stage, where it is scheduled to face Japan.
With both squads packed with established international names and promising youngsters, the BCCI's priority will now be to ensure that logistical concerns do not affect India's bid to retain both Asian Games cricket titles.
Indian Squads at Asian Games 2026:
- Indian men's team: Shreyas Iyer (captain), Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Ishan Kishan, Shivam Dube, Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakravarthy, Ravi Bishnoi, Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
- Indian women's team: Harmanpreet Kaur (captain), Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh, Gunalan Kamalini, Bharti Fulmali, Sree Charani, Renuka Thakur, Kranti Gaud, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav, Nandani Sharma.
